title: Buxa's runaway tigress 'Dooars Rani' captured in Assam, being brought back to Bengal
dek: The three-year-old tigress, released into Buxa Tiger Reserve on October 2, was tranquilised in Kokrajhar on Tuesday, 11 days after she swam across the Sankosh into Assam.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Forest teams from West Bengal and Assam captured the tigress that wandered out of Buxa Tiger Reserve on Tuesday, ending an 11-day search in Assam's Kokrajhar district. She was tranquilised and is being taken back by road to Buxa in Alipurduar district, a Bengali daily reported.

The three-year-old tigress, tagged BTR TF-1 and nicknamed "Dooars Rani", was cornered at Gelaguri Gaon, about 10 km from Kokrajhar town in the Bodoland Territorial Region, a newspaper in Assam reported. Teams used four elephants and several excavators to hem her in after she slipped past them for hours. The National Tiger Conservation Authority approved the tranquilisation plan on Monday, the Bengali daily said.

## How the capture unfolded

West Bengal Forest Minister Manoj Oraon, who travelled to Assam to oversee the operation, said the team "searched for her for two hours straight but couldn't find her" before she was finally cornered, according to the Assam newspaper. "Today, we will get our Dooars Rani home," he said, and thanked the people of Assam for their cooperation.

The Kokrajhar district administration had declared a 5-km zone around Gelaguri a restricted area after she was sighted there. Over her journey of nearly 100 km from Buxa, she killed three domestic pigs and four piglets near Hatigarh village, the paper reported. No attacks on people were reported. Reports differed on some details: the Bengali daily placed the capture in the Dotma area of the district.

Officials have not said whether she will go back into the open forest straight away or first be kept in an enclosure at Buxa, or what will be done to stop her straying again. Her radio collar, which let both states follow her through Raimona and the farmland beyond, will remain the main way to track her once she is released.

## How she got there

The tigress, about three years old, was brought from Bihar's Valmiki Tiger Reserve and released into Buxa on October 2. Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari attended the release. On October 23 she crossed the Sankosh river and entered Raimona National Park in Assam, apparently in search of territory of her own, officials said.

State Forest Minister Manoj Oraon said on October 30 that the animal had been tracked through her radio collar and that he would travel to Assam soon to coordinate the operation, a news agency reported. Asked whether she would be tranquilised, he said the department would do nothing that could harm her physically.

## Why it matters

Buxa had no resident tiger for nearly a decade until one was spotted in 2021, with only a handful of sightings since, the latest in January 2026. The release is part of the state's Tiger Augmentation and Recovery Project, run with support from the National Tiger Conservation Authority and the Wildlife Institute of India, to rebuild a breeding population in the reserve.

The Sankosh, which she crossed to reach Assam, is the same river that was put under a flood alert late last month after a glacial lake burst upstream in Bhutan.
